text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The leader of Sweden's Left Party, Gudrun Schyman, who admitted to having an alcohol problem is to return to the party on Monday after spending time away dealing with her problem.
- The success of Nordbanken's recent share buy back could tempt other Swedish bank to follow suit.

- A train driver was arrested in Stockholm after he was found drunk in charge of a train. He missed some stations, put on the emergency brakes at full speed and backed into a station he had just missed.
- Sweden's domestic air traffic is demanding that the Swedish government refund them for the environmental taxes the airlines paid when Sweden joined the European Union.
- A local political party has been established in Stockholm to fight the government over plans to build extensive tunnels under Stockholm city for car and rail traffic.

- Uncertainty surrounding the role of Sweden's Fiba Nordic Securities in the Morgan Grenfell investment scandal could spill over and damage foreign investors' confidence in both the Swedish and the Scandinavian markets, says brokerage house Carnegie.

- Volvo and Mitsubishi are teaming up to improve the environment, cars' performance and their bottom lines. Volvo plans to start installing Mitsubishi direct injection engine in Volvo's V40 and S40 series.
